host.runner: Linux helper container (node 22 bookworm + Docker CLI) driving the engine socket from a VM path; development hostnames via the managed hosts block and a loopback forwarder

keycloak-realm-convergence healthcheck retries raised from 48 to 120 in the drill copy only: realm convergence took about 4.5 minutes here, just past the 4.25-minute budget

recurring_drill.result: failed after 52 seconds and recorded that failure correctly (JSON record plus synveda_pitr_drill_success 0)
recurring_drill.observed: pgBackRest restore completed in 16.9 s; Compose up --wait then ended with container ...-keycloak-database-bootstrap-1 exited (0) and the lifecycle kept the target lock as designed; the same pitr-restore step passed in both restores above, so the failure is intermittent and its cause is not isolated
recurring_drill.cleanup: down and confirmed reset of the restored drill target then succeeded with PITR enabled

defects_found_and_fixed: pitr-backup connected as a nonexistent postgres role (fixed earlier with --pg1-user)
two bootstrap services built the shared PostgreSQL tag but only one selected the pitr target, so PostgreSQL could start without pgBackRest (exit 127)
Docker Engine 29 stamps enable_ipv4/enable_ipv6 options on networks, so the network preflight and asset contract refused every action on an existing project
the restored-source archive guard also blocked config, down and reset on a restored target
open_findings: Keycloak realm convergence takes about 4.5 minutes on this host, past the 4.25-minute health budget; the first attempt once failed its final projection check and needed a restart
pitr-restore failed once of three live runs when Compose up --wait reported the one-shot keycloak-database-bootstrap exiting 0; not yet reproduced or fixed

the product-demo seed and verify one-shots failed on the restored targets (stages product-demo and retry-review; demo retry-review inspect reported a receipt with no source_event response); the cause is not isolated, so restored targets were checked with direct public-API CLI reads and writes instead
no VedaFlow approve/apply was re-run on a restored target; the write was a Cedar-authorised audited scope create
Knowledge index readiness was not separately measured
